summary: Map pension AML risks, test lifecycle controls and document escalation decisions. Explore this five-day intermediate course and its practical outputs.
lede: Anti-money laundering in pension funds focuses on identifying and controlling exposure across contributions, member records, transfers and benefit payments. For pension compliance officers, administrators and internal auditors, the training covers practical ways to map risks, apply customer due diligence and review payment exceptions. Exercises address control ownership, case records, escalation decisions and management reporting, including sanctions-screening governance and data-quality checks.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who assess, operate, test or report AML controls within pension funds and connected administration or investment activities.
modules: Pension Member CDD and Lifecycle Changes
AML Case Logs and Escalation Decisions
AML Control Testing and Board Reporting
prerequisites: Working knowledge of pension administration, financial services compliance or AML controls is expected. No coding or programming is required.
